page: Microsoft Azure M64ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for extremely large in-memory workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8280L processor with x86_64 architecture, this instance features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with hyperthreading at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. Cache architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 105 MB L3 cache. Memory density is exceptionally high, providing 1792.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 28.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is supported locally with 2199 GB of solid-state drive capacity, while hardware acceleration is absent with zero GPUs.

Benchmark analysis highlights a pronounced divide between single-thread processing and memory-intensive throughput. In single-core evaluation, the instance scores in the bottom 10 percent on Geekbench (892.0) and stress-ng, accompanied by poor throughput in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. In contrast, multi-core and large-block memory performance scale into the middle 50 percent and top 25 percent, respectively. The system achieves 196.25 GB/sec on uncached large-block read operations and handles 40.27 million Redis SET operations per second, reflecting solid parallel memory channels.

Qualitatively, the M64ms provides strong economic efficiency when deployed for environments that specifically demand extreme memory allocations per core rather than peak compute cycles. Workloads bound by single-core speed or CPU-heavy task queues will experience poor cost-to-performance efficiency. However, the substantial local SSD capacity bundled with 1.75 TB of system memory makes it viable for enterprise relational databases, large-scale in-memory stores like Redis and SAP HANA, and memory-intensive ETL operations.
description: Microsoft Azure M64ms is an enterprise-grade memory-optimized virtual machine delivering 1792.0 GB of RAM across 64 dedicated vCPUs. Based on the Intel Xeon 8280L processor running at 2.7 GHz on x86_64 architecture, the system provides 32 physical cores, 105 MB of L3 cache, and 2199 GB of local SSD storage without GPU acceleration. Benchmark testing demonstrates modest single-core throughput, ranking in the lower tiers for single-threaded processing and compression. Conversely, multi-threaded tasks and memory subsystems exhibit solid throughput, highlighted by uncached read memory bandwidth of 196.25 GB/sec and 40.27 million Redis SET operations per second. The server provides strong resource consolidation efficiency for memory-heavy architectures, making it well-matched for massive in-memory databases, large-footprint enterprise caches, and memory-bound ETL workflows.
